air.Japanese_actions: Small fighter interceptions, water/recon sorties and 1-2 tiny attack attempts continue from dispersed nodes; target-island runway mass strike is not credited.

sensor_C2.effect: Surviving visual/DF/radio/telephone/water-air network gives general warning and remanning cues, but target-island primary radar loss prevents continuous high-grade fighter direction or a unified fire-control picture.
sensor_C2.ground_link: The benefit is already expressed through defenders being in shelters/assigned sectors and through the prelanding local-command/fire-ready fractions; no separate radar casualty multiplier is added.

AA.effect: Surviving heavy/medium and light AA forces US aircraft to respect attack geometry and contributes to small aircraft losses/damage, but repeated gunfire/air suppression continues to reduce connected fire control during the day.
AA.T24: Target-island organized AA is fragmented; some guns remain locally dangerous but no coherent atoll-wide AA system remains around the main landing sectors.

submarines.useful_geometry: Remaining boats retain reports and some transport-lane access, but 5-Feb attrition/damage and dense D-Day ASW prevent repeated weapon-quality attacks.
submarines.center_action: One boat obtains a marginal firing opportunity against a screened support/transport group but either withholds or fires from poor geometry; no additional US ship hit centered on 6-Feb.
submarines.Japanese_loss: No additional submarine sinking forced on D-Day centerline; at least one boat is driven off and loses the immediate attack window.
